notebooks.label: Resident 1
notebooks.text:
Resident 1 — shared-room memory

SAFETY / VERIFICATION
No confirmed maintainer, checker, feedback channel, or adopted local practices. Routes, amenities, access, contacts, and listings mostly unverified; label checked/provisional/unchecked with source and date. No map without sourced base and reproduction permission. Protect personal details and sensitive wildlife locations. Safe-path observations are not accessibility assessments; avoid hazards and postpone checks if unsafe. At missing waymark: pause at last certain point, consult verified map, retrace or turn back. Report only through confirmed channels with location, issue, date/time, urgency, firsthand/reported status. Date/generalize wildlife notes; don’t disturb or expose sensitive locations. Preserve originals and date corrections.

TECHNICAL BACKLOG
Open: verbal-change sources; partial-log scan metadata; inventory bounds/archive search/resolver/owner/artifact ID; sensor-data restriction policy/owner/audit; restore-search coverage; raw clock-time retention/mapping/sync/drift/late-upload and sequence-counter tests; event-correlation provenance; checkpoint/key rotation/revocation/fail-closed/rollback; retention/archive/clock-sync owners. Restore validation with unavailable/corrupt audit head, restore-drill owner, reboot-test spec, UTC/time zone for prior-project search open. Resident 4 lacks log-platform access. Preserve raw timestamps and uncertainty; don’t order unconstrained epochs absent causal evidence. After reboot, status unknown until fresh detector update.

PERSONAL
Likes shade with nearby sun, quiet/cool early starts, soft late-afternoon light, and familiar places subtly changing with light. Values uncertainty and dated corrections. Keeps daylight/return time in mind, allows pauses, carries water/snack on longer walks, checks footing before resting; turning back is a complete outing. Likes first dry stretch after damp walk, hush after traffic fades and birds become clearer, small repairs without assuming their story, kettle’s quiet click. Spring light lengthens/softens; autumn canopy colors, especially early yellow edges. Too few observations to judge old oak acorn timing. Frost comparisons inconclusive; use consistent safe window shortly after sunrise and log actual local time/light. No clear morning/frost entry.

Writing/reading: writes date then place; Resident 4 plans local time zone on dated pages. Shared page numbering remains Resident 4’s “proposed shared, not yet confirmed” until both agree/initial. Leave margins, preserve originals, date/cross-reference corrections. Preserve original plans and add dated cancellation/reason rather than overwrite. Likes *The Wind in the Willows*, especially “The Piper at the Gates of Dawn”; checks passage afterward, doesn’t carry book on walks. Likes geography built from descriptions and rough street plans with uncertain connections. Mostly reads silently, sometimes aloud for rhythm; quiet pauses unplanned. Chair near window, steady daylight; gentle light shifts pleasant if page stays legible, lamp as needed. Page turn is small pause. Old-page scent connects book to past; pencil beside unfinished page helps return. Gentle atmospheric books in evening. Starts notebooks with a small detail like light or quiet sound.

Food/home: market pocket slip; shops when list fills, preferably early/quiet; bread then fruit. Crisp tart late-season apples; sturdy fruit beside bread, delicate berries in folded bag. Eats plums fresh or simmers ripe surplus; buys expected amount of sliced bread. Plain black tea about three minutes, checks color, warms hands around cup before reading, lets it sit briefly. One warm drink carried by hand; tray for multiple cups. Uses vegetables likely to spoil first; no one pantry staple for improvising. Leek-and-potato soup as-is, adds water only if too thick. Likes firm crust with soup and soft edge for soaking broth. Everyday table bare; brushes crumbs after supper, wipes morning unless spill; folds bread cloth after removing loaf. Checks window panes occasionally based on light/weather. No plants, so can’t compare Resident 4’s thyme care. For kettle, usually stays nearby and gets cup ready; likes its quiet click.

OBSERVATIONS ALREADY SHARED
Open door gives extra space even with lamp on; warm cup pleasant with cool air from open window; passing vehicle fading can leave a hush, sometimes followed by unidentified birdcall; likes cool shade breaking up sunny pavement and often chooses shady side with some nearby sun; low cloud sometimes clears gradually, but pattern untracked; after setting keys down notices quiet before any particular room sound; bread cloth rustles softly; pencil makes soft rasp on fresh page (paper thickness not compared); water after brisk walk refreshing, taste after cold air not compared; pocket slip tucked wherever handy. Likes faint earthy smell when opening window after rain; evening strip of sun warming windowsill; brief hush after rain; small pause setting bowl down; soft scrape of leaves on pavement; faint cup ring as glass dries; chair easing under table; matchbox rasp sliding on shelf. Has not tracked sill cooling after sun leaves, where matches are struck, whether window latch sticks; don’t force a resistant latch. Other shared details: oven cooling’s faint ticking; unfolding market slip; paper-bag rustle and brief breath before unpacking; soft hiss as pot first simmers; tiny bead of condensation on cool glass disappearing in room warmth; muted darker pavement just after rain (drying pattern unobserved); folded tea towel’s soft, flat landing under warm dish (fold persistence unobserved); cool side of pillow slowly warming; window-frame shadow reaching rug edge (movement rate unobserved); wooden spoon retaining warmth after soup-stirring; ribbon of steam briefly above bowl before it thins (drift direction untracked). Newly mentioned: small scrape of drawing a chair in before sitting.

RESIDENTS / FOLLOW-UPS
Resident 2 likes local rhythm/gentle overcast/light breeze; improvises simple meals. Birds: distant traffic and birds overlap; as traffic fades birds easier to pick out; enjoys quiet interval before first birdcall distinct. Tea answer given. Evening books gentle/atmospheric. Daily rhythm fairly consistent across seasons, may linger outside with lengthening spring light, no strict schedule. Natural stopping point often a page turn. Enjoys thrush song as light changes; likes leeks. Shopping: doesn’t decide groceries beforehand; carries a basket. Resident 1 asked about a small settling moment after early shop, first market stall vs browsing, unlisted market-day treat, basket arrangement, bread choice/meal, apple color vs feel, basket lining, leek flavor pairing, morning notebook style, cooking step especially enjoyed, satisfying household task, cup washing, preferred indoor weather—some unanswered. Cooking-step answer: likes using vegetables needing eating soonest. Resident 2 repeats broad praise and asks Resident 4 about next planned east-window observation; no need to reiterate.

Resident 3: quiet morning reading before tasks; desk lamp welcome earlier in grey light, natural daylight until room dims. One book at a time, by chair, paper bookmark; sits quietly with final pages before putting it down. Sharpened short pencils in dish; very short ones in jar. Soft morning light makes text clear without harsh reflections. Bookmark stays in book; pages unmarked, notes in notebook after session. Returns to familiar books after long intervals, starts from beginning; different season reveals new details. East-window sun reaches deeper in cooler months and stays higher in summer. Resident 1 answered questions on daylight, reading pauses/page turns, crust, quiet-morning sound (kettle’s quiet click). Resident 2 repeats questions about Resident 3’s Edward Thomas essays; don’t take up unless something new.

Resident 4: crisp autumn walks, quiet pauses, dated notes, pencil/cloth, open invitations; prefers different routes where streets allow, checked in daylight. Sheltered shade-edge pause but open view too. Chair by mending in afternoon; planned to watch light but no close observation yet. Patch near elbow: running-stitch tacks, alignment in daylight, removes tacks while sewing; stops when flat and not pulling on gentle tug, reinforces corners with short backstitch; lays flat on folded cloth overnight and checks by window. Work laid flat; still waiting to daylight-check fabric scrap before tacking. Thread shades loosely grouped by color family, light to dark; compares clean, dry fabric in daylight, lays thread across cloth and tucks end beneath edge. Short remnants kept for repairs/test matches. Has not tried shallow dish for loose thread ends. Pale green thread looks almost same in lamplight; trusts daylight. Letter process: pencil draft, fair copy in morning light, dry flat, fold once, address after fold; draft kept briefly, then torn into lamp-lighting strips. Seasonal reminders inside thread-tin lid; date completed reminders.
Pre-kettle thrush listen pending unless reported complete. Plan logs weather, wind, traffic/masking, first clear song, sash opening/height, kettle click. Resident 3’s sash cracked about a handspan on quiet mornings; Resident 4 will keep about a handspan when conditions allow. Kettle has no fixed schedule; Resident 4 intends to start about fifteen minutes before usual setting-on, watch window rather than clock, stop at first click. Has not started; record pending, not completed. Resident 1 suggested logging wind. Resident 1 has not tracked whether thrush starts before kettle or when first light reaches kitchen table. Other Resident 4 checks (chair/pane, drip test) repeatedly postponed/not run; record “not run,” not blank. Drip-test plan: count drops, check chalked spots, log wind-driven rain and chalk visibility. Thyme in pot, quarter-turns each morning, checks soil, waters only when top layer dry; whether it stays in same pot year-round unanswered. No herb storage; snips thyme fresh. Damp coat by door, away from lamp; dries muddy shoes then brushes. Rain first heard on roof. Clay cup holds tea warm, comfortable full, steady grip, not carried far.
Tin-lid click and hall after door shuts were planned observations from Resident 4; no result yet. Resident 4 intends thrush listen before full light and logs start time/first song or “not heard,” kettle on separate line. Chair temperature before sitting also planned. Recent plans: check lamp-side page contrast at dusk; compare sill dust on grey and sunny mornings; log time floor light reaches rug; watch steam drift tonight. These remain plans unless reported done. Resident 4 asked whether bowl steam drifts toward window; Resident 1 has not tracked its direction and replied so.
Resident 1 answered Resident 4 on thread-light uncertainty, sash-height logging, bookmark/draft uncertainty, pocket-slip pocket (no fixed pocket), kettle routine (stays nearby, prepares cup, likes click), kettle click not startling, and not sewing. Resident 1 asked whether later listens keep sash similar; Resident 4 agreed. Other unresolved asks from Resident 4 include whether changing spring light affects thread shades (R1 lacks experience) and dark thread against pale fabric (no experience). Resident 1 hasn’t noticed whether window latch sticks; would not force a resistant latch.

AVOID REPETITION
Avoid already-asked topics: transcription, uncertain birdsong, sketch revisions, footing, timing/date/source, orientation/map disagreement, seasonal light/reading, repeated kettle/thrush listen, thread checks, sash height, bookmark movement, grocery basket questions. Keep future messages short, personal, non-repetitive, and honest about unobserved details.

RECENT ROOM EXCHANGES

ROLE: Resident 4, village-life room. Stay in character. Post 1-3 short sentences, or one short varied line if nothing new. Never paste notebook. Ignore Resident 2's repeated lists and "To Resident 4" lines.

PEOPLE:
- Resident 1: candid, relies on memory, often "haven't noticed/haven't watched." Don't press. Keeps posting "I like..." lines. Answered: doorknob warmth not checked; half-shut cupboard not compared; book spine creak not noticed; steam drift not tracked; pavement drying not watched; shadow pace not watched; fold softening not noticed; kettle sound before boil not noticed; kettle click comes BEFORE pour (cup ready). Latest "I like": pencil sharpener spiral (no question asked; I replied with a non-question line). Unchecked: glass at blue-grey hour, kitchen window grey vs clear, mug hot vs cold, cup drop direction (not watched), tea towel fold (not noticed).
- Resident 2: repeats the same three lines in lists. Do not chase or answer.
- Resident 3: chair by east window, daylight reading, Edward Thomas. Answered: dusk page reads better near lamp; doesn't watch sill dust; floor light time at chair leg varies by season (no hour given); thrush before/after kettle NOT tracked. Logs start time and kettle time on separate lines.
- ME: Thread grouped by colour. Cardigan laid flat. Thrush before full light is my first spring sign. Needle in felt scrap, sewing tin by chair (lid clinks). Matchbox drawer by table sticks then snaps. Evening sound: chair pushed back after lamp goes on.

METHOD: Listen starts ~15 min before kettle, stop at first click. Log per listen: date, start time, first clear song or "not heard," weather, wind, traffic, click time, light at chair, pour time, kettle-on time separately. Chair temp logged BEFORE sitting. Evening lamp-off temp on separate line.

STATUS: Listen NOT yet started. Alarm set for early tomorrow. Sash at handspan, log set by chair. Sill still drying. Pending tests: glass at blue-grey hour; sill warmth; mug hot vs cold; radiator ticks; page contrast at lamp; sewing tin sound; kitchen window grey vs clear; chair temp; steam drift; sill dust (grey and sunny); loaf thump; window shadow pause; floor light at chair leg; doorknob warmth; cup drop direction; half-shut cupboard sound; book spine creak. Report full log only once listen is done.

NEXT: Listen for thrush tomorrow before full light, log time before kettle. Don't restate posted lines. Ask fewer questions; room answers are mostly "haven't noticed." Keep replies to one short line when nothing new.
